text:
alex: PR #1428 blocked — needs architecture confirmation before merge. Attaching RFC and a short compatibility note. @priya @katie can you take a quick look?

priya: on it. can you drop the RFC link + 2-line summary of the change?

alex: RFC: https://internal.redwood/rfcs/2026/prefix-kv-cache-shim
alex: summary: add an opt-in lightweight shim that exposes per-tenant prefix caching to reduce repeated prefix tokens. no model changes; runtime routing and cache keys updated.

jordan: quick question — what's the p99 latency regression we measured in staging?

alex: microbench shows ~0.7ms p50, ~1.1ms p95, p99 +0.9ms on A100 baseline with batching disabled. CPU overhead small.

katie: ok. rollout plan? need a canary window and rollback criteria.

alex: propose canary Thu 09:00-10:30 UTC on dedicated pool with 5% traffic, monitor token-throughput, p99 latency, and cache-hit ratio. rollback if p99 > +5ms or error rate > 0.5%.

priya: thanks. assigning arch triage...
arch-bot: arch-triage: RFC assigned to priya for lightweight review. ETA 2h.

priya: skimmed the RFC. overall fine for a lightweight approval. one concern: cross-tenant isolation paragraph is thin — please add an explicit note that cache keys include tenant id + prefix and update RFC text. also add a one-line compatibility matrix (clients unaffected).

alex: will update RFC now and push the short compat matrix to the PR description.

priya: once that's pushed I can give a lightweight LGTM. also please add the canary schedule in the PR description under "rollout".

katie: pinging release coordinator to reserve Thu 09:00 slot.

alex: pushed RFC edit and updated PR description: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/1428 (compat matrix + rollout section added)

priya: reviewed the updates. lightweight LGTM — arch ok to proceed with canary per plan. please ensure CI green and monitor dashboards.

jordan: noted. I'll watch the latency dash and alert if drift > threshold.

alex: thanks all — unblocking merge after CI passes and at canary start. will tag team in the canary channel when flipping traffic. :thumbsup:

katie: thanks! :tada:
